other.text: Observations carry no feature of interest; they reach the machine through the sensor and the own property am:isAttachedToMachine. sosa:Sensor and sosa:Actuator are declared subclasses of an own am:Device class to keep OWL 2 RL.

Observations subclassed per property instance (irrig:Soil30cmDepthMoistureObservation…). caso:Observation marks aggregations with prov:wasInformedBy to its inputs, caso:Deduction gives a caso:State as result.
A DUL-aligned pattern network: observations express states (se-situ:State) and situations; a configuration procedure (subclass of sosa:Procedure) per sensor; TBox only, no instance data shown.
Sample chain in the case study: a sampling of room air gives the sample air, which is then the feature of interest of the observation. Adds own DeviceId and hasSubDevice to the SSN classes.
Deployments stand for areas of a laboratory (ssn:WestSideMaldiTof), and the work mints its own individuals in the ssn: namespace (ssn:SN_22, ssn:DHT22_22).

Alignment axioms only (SOSA to PROV-O, OBOE, BCO/OBI/BFO), no instance data. oboe:Measurement is made equivalent to sosa:Observation and an OBOE observation groups measurements through rdfs:member; ssn:Property is aligned to bfo:Quality.

SOSA properties are borrowed onto own classes bfp:Observation and bfp:Record (a device status), with no sosa:Observation or sosa:Sensor; devices link to their observations by own bfp:hasObservation / bfp:hasRecord.
SWRL privacy rules over observations, which are matched to terms of service by an own string observation_name and given data categories and privacy rules.
New relations are minted in the sosa namespace (sosa:close, sosa:hasSpatial, sosa:hasTemporal) and inferred by SWRL rules; reconstructed values are a subclass of sosa:Observation.
Collection-level metadata: properties set on an ObservationCollection (result, feature of interest) are shared by its members; the feature of interest comes from an external vocabulary (OIEAU).
The IotStream is the root node that carries sensor, quantity kind, unit, location and quality, so stream observations stay minimal; observations can be outputs of an analytics process.
Observations of virtual and cognitive sensors carry inferred results (activity levels, disease names) about an apartment, chained by stream reasoning.

Measurement samples (DICMeasurementSample, a subclass of sosa:Sample) are the entry point from which observations and results are reached; calibration outputs are linked to procedures with prov:wasGeneratedBy.

Instance IRIs are written under SOSA-like prefixes (sosa:Observation/…, sosa:Sensor/DHT11); each observation carries a blockchain hash and a trustability score, and SHACL shapes check observation quality.
IoT-Lite over SSN 2011 terms (ssn:Sensor, ssn:Device): no observation is modelled, sensors carry quantity kind, unit, location and service; the patient is an iot-lite:Entity.
Restricts the range of sosa:resultTime and sosa:phenomenonTime to own transaction-time and valid-time classes; humans and social media are treated as sensors.
Observations link to their monitoring station by an own property (MonitoringStation) rather than through a sensor or feature of interest; SQWRL rules raise pollution alerts over observations.
sosa:Platform is made equivalent to WoR:Environment, and devices and platforms expose Web resources through an own Exposes relation; no observation data shown.
Mobility stations, vehicles and charging columns are themselves sensors; their sensor records bundle a state (SKOS concept), a timestamp and a series of sosa:Observation.
Multi-typing: a musical instrument individual is at once an iot:Thing, mo:Instrument, prov:Entity and sosa:Platform.
Entity-level alignment of a property-graph model: a SensorProperty entity is aligned with ssn:Observation, and an IoT platform with ssn:System.
Instance IRIs are minted under the specification URL (https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/Sensor{col3}); a toy weather example for table-to-graph mapping.
Quality-of-data indicators are a subclass of ssn:SystemProperty, each with metrics and interpretations, in JSON-LD.
Observations are subclassed by value type (BooleanObservation, DoubleValueObservation), and sensor classes carry axioms fixing what they observe and which observations they make.

The PLC is both a platform hosting sensors and actuators and a system implementing the control procedure, whose input is an observation; attacks compromise features of interest and violate own SafetyProperty nodes.
Jena rules propagate the location of a platform to the subsystems of its deployed system, and shortcut the result chain into an own hasObservationValue.
SSN terms are re-declared in an own ex: namespace (ex:Sensor, ex:observedProperty, ex:onPlatform), with observedProperty on the sensor.
Built on SSN 2011 (ssnx namespace); the observation IRI embeds the indicator and the month (ex:NoiseSensorObservation_LdInterval201704) for a monthly average.
Properties carry the expected value type (semic:observationType / actionType) and static properties hold literal values; sosa:Sensor is split into physical and virtual (software) sensors.
Devices are ssn:System individuals whose continuous behaviour is given by ODE records; variables carry an ssn:symbol property that SSN does not define.
The work mints its own individuals in the ssn: namespace (ssn:AoxMercury, ssn:TVOC).
sosa:madeBySensor is attached to a qudt:Quantity data set in JSON metadata of an HDF5 file, with no sosa:Observation; uncertainty given by qudt:standardUncertainty.
Quality-of-context indicators (precision, freshness) are attached to the sensor output of each observation.
A textbook example in which the device is a platform hosting its sensing element; the observation shown has no sensor or property link.
Reuses SSN 2011 through the Global City Indicator Pollution ontology: concentrations link directly to the weather station by ssn:isProducedBy, keeping raw and calibrated values side by side.
Dataset metadata distinguish the feature of interest (the sample) from the ultimate feature of interest (the sampled real-world phenomenon) of ssn-ext, to support domain-neutral search.

A material sample (sosa:Sample) is the centre of the schema, with a sampling event, a sampling site for the spatial context, curation activities and relations to other resources; a LinkML schema, no RDF instance shown.
The observation module is centred on FeatureOfInterest and ObservationValue (an SSN 2011 class) mixed with SOSA, OWL-Time and OM/QUDT terms.

Sensors are linked to their observations through a hasResult relation, and threshold readings are tied to building components by an own ContainedIn relation; SOSA is aligned rather than reused directly.
Capability attributes take instances or classes as domain and range (unioned with rdfs:Class), revising SSN 2011 measurement capabilities with conditional accuracy.
SSN 2011 terms are paraphrased; features of interest are equated with agricultural conditions (weather, water, soil).
The fused value and its standard deviation go on the result (qudt:standardUncertainty); observations are then translated into logical facts for regulation checking.
Tutorial example: oven temperature observations about a pizza (feature of interest by UUID) with no sensor, property or time triple; the time is in the stream element IRI.
Observations link to the weather station by an own property wep:madeByStation instead of a sensor, and are subclassed (weo:MeteorologicalObservation).
Environmental monitoring stations are modelled as sosa:Sampler and their time series as sosa:Sampling, rather than sensors and observations, with per-pollutant value properties.
Procedures described as plans: EP-Plan plans extend ssn:Procedure (P-Plan lineage) and are aligned with the device (ssn:System) that follows them.
Context attributes (user activity, location, emotion) are made equivalent to sosa:Observation.
SWRL rules over observations assign alarm levels from alarm ranges attached to observable properties, and combine nearby alarms with custom geo built-ins.

Own classes declared equivalent to SOSA ones (ucsn:DataValue to sosa:Observation, ucsn:SensedInformation to sosa:ObservableProperty), with a sensing status per property recording sharing with data consumers; past locations of mobile sensors.
The feature of interest is a node per property and location (tempFOI/location/001); about 80 to 90 triples per observation.
Queries mint terms in the sosa: namespace (sosa:PointID, sosa:Temperature, sosa:MuseumPoint) and attach sosa:hasResult directly to properties (udeo:availableBikeNumber sosa:hasResult ?x).

Observations subclassed per modality (TimeSeriesObservation, ImageObservation, ComputedObservation derivedFrom sources); SWRL rules compare simple results with specification limits bound to the same observable property; DetectionMethod subclasses sosa:Procedure.
Own foo: copies of SOSA classes aligned by owl:equivalentClass; observable properties double as datatype properties carrying values; trail-camera images given by a path URI.

Access permissions are attached to observable and actuatable properties rather than to observations; ssn-system property subclasses carry values via dul:hasDataValue; observation quality as subclasses (Poor, Fair, Good).
madeLastObservation is a subproperty of sosa:madeObservation for the latest result; sosa:hosts relates appliances to ingredients they contain; SWRL rules pick the actuator for a cooking step.
Features of interest are locations (station site, hypocentre); a data point has one to three axis components; collections of collections (matrix of arrays).

Observations subclassed per theme (kwg-ont:VulnerabilityObservation); census and survey statistics modelled as observations of regions and S2 cells; integration through the spatial feature rather than shared properties.

Each observable property declares the observation type it takes as value (semic:observationType), observations are subclassed per type (occupancy observations), and static properties hold literal values.

Observations are also ewe:Events, actuations ewe:Actions and results ewe:Parameters (task automation); one property class is a subclass of both ObservableProperty and ActuatableProperty; actuators use sosa:forProperty.
Observations subclassed by epistemic level (EvidenceObservation, PerceivedHazardObservation, PropertyEstimation); reliability attached to results; revisable estimated event states with OWL-Time.

Own ofo: copy of the sensor pattern (Wearable, Feedback, Property, FeatureOfInterest) aligned to SOSA; results may attach to feedback, property or feature; time series stay in InfluxDB behind data points.
Quality-of-context criteria and min/max interpretation thresholds are attached to observable properties.
Sensor functions are sosa:Procedures with ssn:Input/ssn:Output arguments; SHACL metadata profiles validate every node; system parameters are ssn:Property of components.
The feature of interest is a location node (location/001); about 80 to 90 triples per observation.
Stations are subclasses of both sosa:Platform and geo:Feature; an interpolator ssn:System is hosted on grid-cell platforms; the graph is virtual (Ontop mappings over SQL).

Observations are subclassed per kind (SpatialPositionObservation, SafetyDistanceObservation from 3D simulation, CVPeopleNumObservation from video AI) and sosa:Observation is itself a subclass of ctx:ExternalContext; quantities are separate qudt:Quantity nodes with unit:KiloGM.
Queries use 2011 SSN terms (observedBy, observationResultTime, hasValue) under the 2017 ssn: namespace, with iot-lite for quantity kinds and devices.

Feature, phenomenon time and provenance (raster file) sit on the collection, members carry only property and result; collections are also dcat:Dataset and prov:Entity; feature is a version of a territorial parcel.
A storm track is a collection of tracklet collections, each tracklet a sample point with time, location and observed attributes; damage types are observed properties of storm events.
An elephant's GPS position is modelled as the result of an observation of an invented sosa:Location property.
2011 SSN with measurement capabilities (accuracy, sensitivity as rdf:value) per device; dynamic properties such as the last measure attached directly to the sensor resource.
2011 SSN with iot-lite: ssn:Device subdivided into sensing and actuating devices; medical objects contain devices and carry own has-location and has-time properties.
A knowledge graph merging 2011 SSN and SOSA terms, choosing ssn:Property over sosa:ObservableProperty as the property class.
Only class alignments between ontologies (SSN/SOSA Sensor, Procedure and FeatureOfInterest made equivalent to OEMA, OntoWind and SAREF classes); no instance data shown.
SWRL-style rules classify observations into derived classes (TrustedObservations, ObservationToHighLevelEnergy) and attach trust values to entities.
SAREF and SOSA combined: measurements subclassed per quantity (IndoorTemperatureMeasurement) carry sosa:hasSimpleResult; SWRL rules compare them with occupants' comfort settings to set actuators.
Per-quantity object properties (hasTemperature, hasPressure, hasWindForce, belongsObservation) and value data properties replace the generic observedProperty pattern.
MQTT packets mapped to SOSA terms: grip position and correction points as properties, actuation signals with correction offsets as simple results.

Readings below the threshold are not stored, so the collection carries aggregate statistics (average, count); constraint evaluations (EP-Plan) are based on the collection; observations are also prov:Activity.
SOSA, QUDT and D-SI terms used as keys of JSON metadata attached to HDF5-style data groups, with madeBySensor pointing to a string.
Calibrated sensors carry a dynamic transfer model whose parameters have units and uncertainties, with covariance matrices encoded in MathML.

SOSA/SSN reduced to a flat event-log schema: observable and actuatable properties merged into one Property, Platform and Deployment merged into a Location concept, feature of interest replaced by the business object of the OCEL log.
The patient wearing a sensor is modelled as the platform that hosts it; situations detected by C-SPARQL aggregates over windows.
sosa:hosts/isHostedBy inside WoT Thing Descriptions drive the URI hierarchy of Solid pod containers.
The IoT-Stream extension adds stream entities between sensors and observations for search and indexing.
Observations are typed per quantity with a class minted in the sosa: namespace (sosa:HeartRateObservation); no observedProperty is given.
SOSA/SSN names reused as annotation values in an XES event-log extension (system type, interaction type), with sosa:Sampling read as a set of subsequent observations.
Observations produced by RML mappings from JSON outputs of ML anomaly-detection modules.
2011 SSN output/value pattern (SensorOutput, ObservationValue, isProducedBy) specialised per quantity (TrafficIntensity...).
The feature of interest is a location node whose IRI encodes the coordinates (oim-feat:loc_70.41_0.0).
The query links sensors to observations with sosa:observes instead of madeObservation; unit heterogeneity (bar, hectopascal) resolved at query time.
Calibrated-sensor classes combine SOSA with the digital SI model (D-SI) for measurement uncertainty and calibration models.
An RL agent annotates environment streams with SSN observations of process properties (waiting time of an order).
Factorized observations: identical readings at different timestamps are represented once, to shrink the knowledge graph built on demand from a stream.
Observation and its OM measure merged into one instance typed sosa:Observation and om:Measure.
Models written in YAML and converted to N-Quads to generate edge deployments.
sosa:isObservedBy links observations to gateways (the property is meant for observable properties); observations are presence intervals derived from image interpretation.
New sensor types are added as ssn:Sensor subclasses to an IoT dictionary built by knowledge extraction.
N3 rules generate sensor queries; uses a non-SOSA sosa:hasObservation linking a sensor to observations that carry symptoms.
Actuations target an ActuatableProperty such as Email and are triggered by ContextAwareRules over observations; an actuator executes only one actuation. Gateways and Groups modelled as sosa:Platform.
Observations subclassed per kind (TargetPosition, QualityObservation); quality observations take another observation as feature of interest. Procedures are individuals of a sosa:Procedure taxonomy.

ObservableProperty carries the data type of the observed value; each sensor observes one property and each actuator acts on one. Thing extends sosa:Platform; context-awareness rules trigger actuations.
A bridge cross-section is declared a sosa:Platform hosting the sensors installed on it. Observations produced by R2RML mappings and stored in HBase.
Built on the 2011 SSN with DUL: indicators are ssn:SensorOutput and scoring processes are ssn:Sensing with inputs and outputs. Observations satisfy goals expressed by benchmarks.
TBox only: SEAS energy forms beside sosa:ObservableProperty, ethic modes attached to ssn:System, devices linked to sensors by ioto:hasSensor.
Observations attached to stations by wep:madeByStation rather than to sensors; interval classes by duration reused for all observations. Qualitative values as SKOS collections of WMO codes.
The work mints its sensor, property, feature and observation IRIs in the sosa: namespace (sosa:se-0004). Rules over observations in LARS compiled to Flink.

Observations subclassed per theme (VulnerabilityObservation); survey and census data modelled as observations on regions or S2 cells. Integration relies on the spatiotemporal features rather than shared observable properties.
Monitored entities such as machines and patients are typed ssn:System and their sensors are subsystems. Properties are the items of a dashboard recommender.
ssn:hasSubSystem is reused as a generic part-whole relation between industrial entities and concepts generated from data-lake labels (385 links extracted).
The monitored battery cell is a host of its sensors rather than a feature of interest; no hasFeatureOfInterest shown. Anomaly causes derived by rules over pairs of observations.
SOSA is aligned by mapping: sosa:Observation made equivalent to lhr:EnvSSNResource, sosa:madeObservation to a subproperty of lhr:hasResource, sosa:resultTime to lhr:hasObservationDateTime.
Knowledge graph stored as a Neo4j property graph; observation subclassed per property kind (SpatialPositionObservation).
The motor is both platform and feature of interest of its consumption sensor; sensor thresholds (sn4e:maxValue) are stored on the sensor.
Built on the 2011 SSN: sbms:Observation is tied to a BMS data point and key classes carry IDs with owl:hasKey; observed properties split into physical quantity and property domain.
In the generated Jena rules sosa:Sensor is used as a predicate whose value is a sensor kind literal ('Pressure', 'PIR').
Sensor capabilities with SSN systems module (ssn-system:Range, ssn-system:Frequency) whose values use bop:hasSimpleResult; custom ranges inserted by SPARQL for outlier detection.
Feature of interest is a point IRI with lat/long query parameters; spatio-temporal values kept in a time-series database linked through madeBySensor.

The record subject <sosa/sensor/86338> is typed sosa:Weather_Station (a term not in SOSA) yet carries observedProperty and hasSimpleResult; all IRIs minted in the sosa namespace. Tweets modelled as social sensors observing a property.
Weather stations are subclasses of both geosparql:Feature and sosa:Platform; duration-specific interval classes reused for all observations.
Results linked to evidence resources (photos, videos, reports) and data segments; crack states model the temporal evolution of the feature.
One property individual is typed both sosa:ObservableProperty and sosa:ActuatableProperty; Web Things are typed sosa:Sensor or sosa:Actuator to support discovery queries.
Observations and observation collections aligned with an event ontology: collection members as sub-events, wasOriginatedBy as cause event.

Edge devices are sosa:Platform (written <http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa#Platform>), and ssn:Property is used for hardware resources and data volume/velocity/variety capabilities matched against task requirements.
Symbols of a learned timed automaton are typed sosa:Observation or sosa:Actuation; the work writes sosa:ActuableProperty, a term that does not exist.
Own ontology inspired by SOSA: devices point to observations by hasObservation, and the result (people count) is also copied onto the space entity.
Observations are event detections whose results are events, with the detection rule as sosa:Procedure; raw readings stay in InfluxDB and the model links each sensor to its InfluxDB instance.

System capabilities from S3N and the SSN systems module, with RAM and Flash as system properties carrying schema:value and schema:unitCode om:kilobyte; ML model inputs and outputs as subclasses of ssn:Input and ssn:Output.
Observations as blank nodes scoped per message; sosa:resultTime proposed as the version order of a message profile.
Observation, Sensor and Result each subclassed per climate factor (ca:[?]Observation). The work lists sosa:isMadeBySensor, a term that does not exist.
SOSA is mapped into a city information model by SWRL rules (sosa:Sensor(?x) -> cim:Sensor(?x)), and Brick points are linked to sosa:Observation.
Observable features are DUL roles that physical objects play according to sensor deployment; events (LowTemperature) derived by rules over observations, built on the 2011 SSN.
Process-mining event log entries are modelled as a subclass of sosa:Result with case, activity and timestamp attributes.
Properties are dereferenceable time-varying resources holding the current value; instances of sosa:ActuatableProperty are writable by agents. Brick aligned with SOSA/SSN.
giri:System is a subclass of sosa:System grouping ICT devices, power and cooling subsystems; observations feed sustainability metric instances, and capacities use qudt:QuantityValue.
The stream is an ssn:Output of a sensing; the observation is also a vsd:TimeVaryingGraph and event:Event. Example built on the 2011 SSN with SAO.
Station classes are subclasses of both sosa:Platform and geo:Feature, populated through a virtual knowledge graph over relational data.
Own relations (:isObservationFor, :isObservedPropertyFor, :isDataSourceFor) link hazards, observations, observed properties and data sources.
Measurements stored as (feature, property, time, value) tuples in a time-series database and mapped to SOSA observations on demand (Linked Time Series Data).
Services are mapped to sosa:Sensor and sosa:Actuator and compute-continuum nodes to sosa:Platform in the base TBox.
Observations carry key-value tags (<hasTags>, <keyTag>, <keyValue>) used to select time series for AI services.
ssn:Property is used for design parameters of HVAC components (nominal power, nominal efficiency), alongside BOT, PROPS and FSO.
OM classes are declared subtypes of sosa:Result.
ssn:hasProperty links objects of video scenes to their characteristics in a causal knowledge graph.

Observation subclasses per property and feature defined by necessary and sufficient conditions (irrig:Soil30cmDepthMoistureObservation); deductions as caso:Observation subclasses linked to inputs with prov:wasInformedBy; software computing averages typed sosa:Sensor.

The work proposes its own BOP ontology (bop:Executor, bop:Execution, bop:Property, bop:FeatureOfInterest) generalising the SOSA pattern, with bop:hasSimpleResult and property levels, rather than instantiating SOSA.

The ontology invents SOSA names (sosa:Observable, sosa:hasmadeBySensor, sosa:Longitude) and makes Observation a subclass of feature of interest; procedures subclassed into Actuation, Sampling, Publishing, Composing.
Stream services (enrich, aggregation, join) modelled as auxiliary ssn:SensingDevice instances cloned from input sensors; time granularity via ssn:ResponseTime measurement property with a unit.
Observations linked to executed process tasks by a CONSTRUCT rule (meta:observedOn) comparing resultTime with task start and end on the hosting platform.
Quality of Observation attributes (qoo:hasQoO) attached to observation values; virtual sensors described with SSN capabilities.
Sensor subclasses for mobility (hssn:MobileSensor, hssn:StaticSensor) and a coverage area per sensor, tracked over time with past coverage areas and OWL-Time entities.
Actuations with a feature of interest (light, window) and stream rules deriving user events (closeTo, stoppedFrom) from observations.
Social media users treated as social sensors (sosa:Sensor) and tweets annotated with sosa:resultTime and the property they report on.
Observation subclasses per quantity (EnvironmentTemperatureObservation) and a local aal:madeBySensor subproperty used in place of sosa:madeBySensor.
sosa:phenomenonTime used on features of interest to date planting and presence; experimental plots as sosa:Sample; Jena rules derived from properties.

Observation subclasses (HeartObservation, MovementObservation, WalkingFeature) defined by OWL equivalent-class restrictions on observedProperty and feature, so DL reasoning classifies observations; features are abstract individuals (movement, heart) and observations are interpreted through DUL situations.

Neural network models described as S3N procedures with ssn:hasInput/hasOutput and procedure features whose conditions (RAM, Flash) carry schema:value and schema:unitCode with OM units; matching models to devices by system capabilities.
Per-observation quality assessment results (IDQA vocabulary) attached to sosa:Observation as data properties after SHACL validation.
sosa:observes on the sensor used to determine the sensor type; SOSA/IoTStream entities stored in an NGSI-LD broker.
Replaces sosa:actsOnProperty with an own 'actsOn' relation between Actuator and ActuableProperty after its reasoner inferred Actuation and Actuator equivalent.
Machines of a digital twin ontology composed of SOSA sensors, actuators and platforms, with events as machine outputs.
ioe:System subclasses ssn:System; agents' preferences are defined on an ssn:Property measured in a site, with a preferred value.
sosa:Sensor and sosa:Platform used only as prov:Agent of the activity that generated a dataset (DCAT, Data Cube), with no observations.
Observation and sensor output subclasses per quantity (em:PolyphaseVoltageObservation); stream queries construct alert events typed with DUL.

veo:Device is declared a subclass of both sosa:ObservableProperty and sosa:Sampler, and sosa:Sensor is said to represent a feature measured by the network; sosa:Platform specialised as a seismic network.
IoT devices modelled as a subclass of sosa:Platform inside a privacy preference ontology, with no observations.
Each observation identified by a 32-character id; the observation carries value and date as data properties.
Track_Section declared a subclass of ssn:Platform and signalling elements subclasses of ssn:SensingDevice, composed through DUL:hasComponent restrictions in a railway layout ontology.
Names an own class in the sosa namespace (sosa:ObservableVehicleProperty) and own relations observesVehicleProperty; ADAS as ssn:System subclass for forensic investigation.
sosa:hasSimpleResult applied to the result node rather than the observation; Jena rules over observations for fault detection and control, with Brick points.
Sensor results linked to inputs of control logic through SEAS communication connections; checking observations against the measurement range of the sensor model.
Raster analysis outputs turned into per-territory observations, with provenance to the source raster through prov:wasDerivedFrom.
sosa:isHostedBy combined with an own hasComponent hierarchy to trace anomalous data streams back to components and failure modes.
Assets of a production chain described as accomplishing procedures whose results trigger events; no SOSA instance data shown.
Observation IRIs minted from the device metric path plus a timestamp by RML streaming mappings.
Each dataset record (soil sample, image, GPS fix) becomes an observation individual (Soil_ID, Image_ID); taxonomy classes used for animal features.
SOSA classes used only as qb:concept of Data Cube dimensions and measures, combined with SKOS concepts.
Legacy SSN extended with a wearable sensor platform subclass placed on body parts, aligned with BFO and HL7 FHIR.
Observations and sensor descriptions are stored in two graphs of an IoT registry, joined through the identifier of the sensor (legacy SSN).
A bus stop in a route is modelled as a sosa:Sensor, and expected arrival times as observations whose feature of interest is the stop.
Observations are stream events whose materialised inferences are cached by structure; sensors and properties are static background knowledge.
An own class of collections of EV registrations (ev-ont:ElectricVehicleRegistrationCollection) modelled on sosa:ObservationCollection, without SOSA observations.
CSV on the Web metadata maps middleware CSV rows to legacy SSN observations, minting IRIs from sensor and time columns.
Detected bounding boxes linked to tracked objects with sosa:isSampleOf, asserted by soft ASP rules for video stream fusion.
RDF-star detection and tracking triples annotated with sosa:resultTime (frame index) and a score, without sosa:Observation individuals.
Property IRIs invented in the ssn namespace; IFC devices linked to sensors by ssn:observedBy.
Lists ssn:PowerConsumption among SSN core entities, a term that SSN does not define, with legacy ssn:ObservationValue and ssn:SensorOutput.
Maps its SensorObservationValue concept to sosa:SensorOutput, a term SOSA does not define.
Attributes of grid-cell features modelled as observations in an ontology design pattern, with RCC8 spatial relations between features.
sosa:Procedure used for the steps of actuations; locations of physical entities through a geo:Location class that GeoSPARQL does not define.
ssn:hasProperty links objects of video scenes to their characteristics in a causal knowledge graph, outside any sensing context.
Device descriptions as ontology templates whose subsystems (ssn:hasSubSystem) and producible observations are declared by class restrictions.
The work models IoT measurements with SAREF (saref:Measurement, saref:hasValue, saref:isMeasuredIn), not SOSA/SSN; SOSA is only compared and declared as a prefix.
Observations are subclassed per sensing modality and per satellite product (GIFAPAR_S3_Observation); sosa:Platform declared a subclass of geosparql:Feature.
Zones and devices are subclasses of a platform and nest through sosa:hosts; quality indicators are attached to observations or sensors.
Features of a cyber-threat ontology are mapped to SOSA classes (Observation, Actuation, Procedure, Platform).
Social media posts are modelled as observations made by users as sensors.
Observations are also EWE events and actuations EWE actions (vlctas:ObservedEvent, vlctas:TriggeredAction) for rule-based automation; the property class is both observable and actuatable.
Sensor capabilities with ssn-system:Accuracy, Resolution and Condition using schema:unitCode; thresholds attached to carrier properties and SPARQL rules annotating exceedances.

A merged vehicle observation carries several values (speed, acceleration) through subproperties of hasSimpleResult; road sections are a subclass of sosa:Sample linked by a subproperty of sosa:hasSample.
The feature of interest of fault-detection observations is a sensor itself; actuations produce system states with own timespans, inserted by SPARQL Update rules.
Sensors and actuators are linked to AADL device components, and SWRL rules characterise them.
Rules infer a characteristic index (NDVI, NDWI) of an image from the bands it observes; CharacteristicIndex is an ssn:Property that is not observable.

Continuous sensing and actuation activities (ado:SensingActivity) are linked by own properties instead of sosa:observedProperty / madeBySensor, to avoid being inferred as observations; sensors and actuators are aligned as ep-plan:Agent.
Uses SSN 2011: one observation has several results typed by the quantity (CloudCover, AtmosphPress) instead of an observed property.
The manufacturer's normal output range is an ssn-system:MeasurementRange capability; a robot path is a procedure linked to the sensor by ssn:implements, used to choose a fallback sensor.
Instrument interfaces are platforms that host sensors and actuators, while the instrument links its components by an own property.
Sensors are omitted when no data layer describes them; observations are validated with generic SOSA-SHACL shapes.
Property chains compose sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest with spatial relations to S2 grid cells, which act as features for gridded data.
Observable properties carry the file locations of acceptance limits and results; observations link to test reports by an own property.
Observations (user inputs or meter readings) feed a PROV chain of emission calculation steps; the quantity kind sits on the result rather than an observed property.
The hall is at once a sample of the building, a feature of interest and a platform hosting the sensor board.
Uses SSN 2011: a measurement (control point) observation has per-phenomenon observations as parts via dul:hasPart.
Observations are the data source of KPI calculations; sensors are left out of the model.
A sosa:Result may be an RDF graph description presented with lifting, lowering and validation rules; WoT TD terms are aligned as subclasses and subproperties of SSN system and procedure terms.

In a MERODE domain model, a Device class generalises Sensor and Actuator and a Device Usage class generalises Observation, Actuation and Sampling; an own Platform Deployment ties a platform to one feature of interest.
Observations declare neither unit nor observed property; both are factored on the sosa:ObservationCollection they belong to.
Rules over observations derive new facts (off-limit areas); an observation result can be a person IRI.
The feature of interest is used to hold the sensor and actuator limits and faulty patterns against which observations are compared; Sampling stores observations over a period.
The patient is the feature of interest of the observations, queried through sosa:isFeatureOfInterestOf.
SSN 2011-based observation capability ontology: sensors subclassed into remote and in-situ sensors, linked to tasks and ssn:Stimulus as DUL events.
Own System, Sensor and Actuator classes subclass the SOSA ones, with system components, states, and operating conditions declared subclasses of a sosa:Condition class that SOSA does not define.
Terms are invented in the ssn namespace: ssn:Temperature, ssn:WindSpeed, ssn:relativehumidity as datatype properties.
sosa:Sensor is declared a subclass of bot:Element so rooms contain sensors; evolving room properties use OPM property states.
Uses SSN 2011 with equivalence axioms to PROV-O (ssn:Observation as prov:Entity, ssn:Process as prov:Activity) so a reasoner materialises provenance.
Only sosa:Procedure and ssn:System are reused, as concepts of a civil complaint ontology for digital-twin government.
The kind of measurement is given by the type of the result node (HeartRateObservationValue) rather than an observed property.
Smart-building algorithms (forecasting, MPC) are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, with their inputs and outputs as subclasses of ssn:Input and ssn:Output linked to Brick sensors.
Datasets are modelled as collections of virtual entities whose primary source is a sensor, linked with PROV-O activities such as measurement campaigns.
Test messages use non-standard SSN terms (ssn:hasID, ssn:hasUnit with qu:DegreeCelsius) as inputs to an automatic mapping system.
An ssn:Deployment stands for a building and is linked to beacons by an own namespace property rather than ssn:deployedSystem.
Quality-of-observation attributes and effects are attached to SSN 2011 measurement capabilities.
Controllers and predictors implement procedures (pep:implements) and optimise properties of HVAC spaces as features of interest.
Domain classes are placed under BFO, QUDT, SOSA and MASON parents; process parameters are QUDT quantity kinds while measured quantities are observable properties.
Spatial relations link sensors, observable properties and bridge components, with space types from SPOT.
A GraphQL interface navigates platform, hosts, madeObservation; the room itself is the platform.
Sensed data are drone:MissionSensorData mission event elements rather than sosa:Observation.
The observation pattern is collapsed into one predicate per property and result time (averageHeatingDegreeDaysPerMonthAug2021) pointing directly to the simple result.
SOSA terms are used as NGSI-LD relationships in JSON-LD entities alongside SAREF4EE and M3-lite properties.
sosa:Observation and saref:Measurement are mapped to the work's own observation and measurement classes for construction quality inspection.
A holdsState data property on the dynamic vehicle property gives the current value without instantiating a sosa:Observation.
Stream payload fields are linked to a sosa:Property (a term SOSA does not define) to tie stream schemas to system capabilities.
IoT sensors themselves are said to act as features of interest for observation and actuation.

Logical sensors/actuators (subclasses of sosa:Sensor/Actuator) run SPARQL software procedures whose executions take observations as ssn:hasInput and produce observations as ssn:hasOutput; the door is both feature of interest and platform.

MCSO aligns to SSN mostly by equivalent classes (loose coupling); observations are grouped by DL-defined subclasses using usedProcedure to a campaign; sensor specifications (resolution, range) carry UO units.
ssn:Observation is aligned as a subclass of prov:Entity and orbac:Object, and sosa:hasResult as a subproperty of prov:generated, for usage-control policies on observations.

Actuators are linked to ssn:Properties through :PropertyChange and :Effect individuals, optimal conditions are OWL class expressions over properties, and Jena rules generate :Actions from actuator states; property values sit on property individuals.
The work mints its own terms in the ssn: namespace (ssn:isMotedBy, ssn:Kitchen, ssn:Mum, ssn:On) and refines ssn:isObservedBy into ssn:isSensedBy and ssn:isMotedBy per sensor kind.
Own terms are minted in the sosa: and owl: namespaces (sosa:hasOccuredAt, owl:hasObservationValue); rooms are platforms; results are activity labels used in SWRL/SQWRL rules.
Logical sensors/actuators (subclasses of sosa:Sensor/Actuator) run software procedures whose executions take observations as ssn:hasInput and produce observations as ssn:hasOutput.

Observations subclassed per quantity (ex:TemperatureObservation); the C-SPARQL queries re-mint SOSA properties in the work's anomaly: namespace (anomaly:hosts, anomaly:madeObservation, anomaly:hasSimpleResult).

Old SSN (ssnx) with observation subclasses per event type (?ob rdfs:subClassOf ssn:Observation); sensors are event services discovered by observed property and feature; location values are observation results.
Individual animals (southern elephant seals) are modelled as sosa:Platform hosting satellite tags; time, space and units are said to use OWL-Time, GeoSPARQL and QUDT but are not shown in data.

Alignment of the W3C Thing Description with SSN: things may be systems, platforms or features of interest, connected devices are modelled as features of interest, and property affordances relate to ssn:Property through ssn:forProperty, inferred from @type tags by rules.

Only SOSA properties are imported, not its classes; observations are subclassed into NumericObservation and StatusObservation, and sensors are linked by own correlation and influence properties for diagnosis.

Observations are workflow activity instances (vpd:SensorActivityInstance subclass of sosa:Observation and wild:ActivityInstance), sensor and machine activities are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, and DCAT datasets link to observations through prov:wasGeneratedBy.
Indoor-positioning observations of workers have locations as their values and are chained by dicp:hasNextObservation; observedProperty points to saref:Property in the SAREF alignment.

Observations are satellite images (sors:SatelliteImage equivalent to sosa:Observation) subclassed per satellite (LandsatImage, SentinelImage, MODISImage); results are subclassed per land-cover percentage.
Informal SSN-like triples with own property names (:observedBy, :observationValue, :time); the user's location is an observation value used by SWRL context rules.
Forecast models are virtual sensors; quantile predictions use 24 sub-properties of sosa:hasSimpleResult (covid-so:point, covid-so:quantile-N).
Old SSN (ssnx) with CF properties; sensors point to a per-plot feature with ssn:ofFeature, and plots link to crop treatments for filtering.
Cyber-twin ontology: machine automation programs and data translators are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, machines link to sensors, actuators and platforms by own properties.
An own observation-like class pdto:AtomicInformation links a product (pdto:hasFeatureOfInterest) and an ssn:Property (pdto:clarifiedProperty) to a value, instead of sosa:Observation.

Data-quality assessments are attached per observation through idqa:qualityOfObservation, a subproperty of ssn-system:qualityOfObservation, after SHACL validation; the IoT device collecting data is called a sosa:Sampler.
A hardware device is one wot:Thing typed both sosa:Sensor and sosa:Actuator; user preferences on WebThings properties are matched to actuators.
Knowledge base overlays merge a building knowledge base (SSN observations) with smartphone knowledge bases so that logical actuators use users' observations and preferences.
Observation classes defined by a value restriction on hasSimpleResult (ex:HighTempObservation) for anomaly classification; sosa:observes points to a unit.
Lightweight stream ontology: StreamObservation (sosa:Observation subclass) carries only values and timestamps, metadata (sensor, unit, quantity kind, location, service) sit on the IotStream.
Machine perception by abduction: ssn:isPropertyOf between properties and features (diseases) is encoded as a bit matrix to explain observed properties.

Detected anomaly events carry the detector as sosa:usedProcedure and point with ssn:wasOriginatedBy to the sensor properties whose time series triggered them; sensor metadata drive dashboard widget selection.
A SWRL rule types the sensor itself as the observation (Observation(?sensor)); SSN/SAN terms are reimported with own properties (hasSpot, hasState, hasValue) and converted to Drools rules.

A meta-context model mixing old SSN (ssn:Device, ssn:SensingDevice), IoT-Lite and an own iot-context vocabulary is populated by an LLM mapping table columns to concepts, to derive functional dependencies for data cleaning.
SOSA and QUDT terms appear as key-value pairs in Avahi (mDNS) service advertisements so that oneM2M devices discover each other without a controller.
Observations are deliberately kept out of the knowledge graph (BIM-IoTDI) to avoid growth; only sensors, properties and rooms are described semantically, with BOT, IFC and Brick.
Actors and human-centricity factors are linked directly to sensors by isObservedBy, and sensors send outputs to an own Data class, without sosa:Observation.

No observedProperty: the quantity is encoded in the observation IRI (urn:dev:mac:…/current, …/voltage), and a sosa:hasUnit term not in SOSA is invented; the JSON-LD serves as a baseline for CBOR templates.
Process steps and transformation processes are subclasses of sosa:Actuation, performed by sosa:Actuator (PO2:Material) with sosa:Procedure (PO2:Method); observations are attached to steps.
An AnonymizationProcedure subclass of sosa:Procedure records how personal information was removed; observations are mapped to access-control Resources.
Signals not produced by any sensor get a vss:VirtualSensor to fit the SOSA pattern; observations are abstracted into step:Episode instances of semantic trajectories by rules.
SSN classes (ObservableProperty, Sensor) are reimplemented as Python graph-object classes stored in Neo4j, with methods named after SSN properties.
Old SSN data published from a relational database with D2RQ mappings that generate both the sensor-type classes and the sensor instances.
RDF-star quoted triples are typed as observations (a frame image, detections, tracklets), each with sosa:usedProcedure pointing to the DNN or tracking algorithm (:Yolo, :KalmanFilter).
sosa:Observation and saref:Measurement are both aligned to an own Observation class; observations are checked against indoor-condition constraints of construction activities.
Old SSN ssn:SensingDevice linked by own properties (mmkg:outputs to data, mmkg:hasMeasuringProperty to an own MeasurementProperty class) in a multimodal scene graph; no sosa:Observation.
Observations are subclassed per type of sensor that generated them (four subclasses) and linked to recognised activities.
Numerical values are kept out of the ontology (time-series store); the ontology describes only measures, features and properties.
qb:Observation is declared equivalent to sosa:Observation, merging Data Cube and SOSA; O&M sampling points are subclasses of geosparql:Point.
Each sensor reading is an LDP RDF source typed ssn:SensorOutput served over CoAP, with no observation node.
SSN/SOSA device instances are combined with GDPRtEXT privacy-by-design concepts.
Old SSN sensors in a process-model knowledge base carry energy-cost attributes as literals containing the unit name, queried with a regex on "milliwatt".
A data acquisition system class (DAS) implements the procedure and is connected to sensors.
Smart musical instruments are platforms hosting sensors and also expose services.
Extends IoT-Stream (StreamObservation, IotStream with sosa:Sensor, QU quantity kind and unit, geo:Point) with patient and health-condition classes.
Observation events carry sensor and timestamp so that precise measurements are fetched from a time-series database on demand.
ssn:hasProperty links objects of video scenes (scene ontology) to their characteristics in a causal knowledge graph used for link prediction.
SWRL rules over observations detect abnormal situations; C-SPARQL stream reasoning over observations; alignment of SOSA to DUL.
SHACL rules compute derived values and aggregates over observations with automatic unit conversion; features are platform parts linked by hasPart.
Neural networks and CEP rules are described as s3n:Algorithm procedures with ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput subclasses and memory requirements as ssn-system conditions, inside WoT Thing Descriptions.
Observations subclassed per domain (EarthquakeObservation, AQObservation); SHACL shapes validate SOSA data, e.g. one sensor per observation collection.
A virtual sensor implements a detection query; events and states derived from observations with causal knowledge between state types and topological relations through hosting.
Mobile sensors whose observations are coordinates (m2ssn:MobileSensor); complex event detection over multimedia sensor observations.
AI models are sosa:Procedure instances with ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput and REST endpoints; controllers typed with invented terms in the sosa namespace (sosa:MachineAutomation, sosa:MachineSetting).
Observations subclassed per quantity (TempValue, HumidityValue, CO2level); sensors linked to observations by own per-quantity properties (:hasSmokeValue); SWRL rules over results raise fire risk.
Virtual sensors and actuators (vhbieo:VirtualSensor) for immersive virtual environments next to in-situ ssn:Sensor; survey answers treated alongside observations as data of an occupant.
Observations subclassed per feature type (RoadObservation, IncidentObservation, ActivityObservation); a shortcut property from road to length besides the observation.
Observations subclassed per meaning and rule outcome (ExhibitProximityObservation, ObservationToHighLevelEnergy) with SWRL rules deciding lamp brightness.
Observation IRIs minted from the OPC UA nodeId and the timestamp; RML stream mapping from OPC UA.
hasSimpleResult mapped as subproperty of domain quantity properties (Length, Volume); SWRL rules over observations infer hazards.
Observations are observedBy the weather station; observation IRIs encode timestamp, station and property; a quality value per observation.
Gateways and LoRa nodes modelled as platforms for connectivity management; hardware vs software sensors.
Cameras are the features of interest of aggregated count observations, the aggregation tool being the sensor; aggregation function given by cot:usingFunction.
Inspections as sosa:Procedure (eurotl:InspectionActivity) used by condition observations; an agent takes the sensor role.
Observations as time-annotated named graphs in RDF streams consumed by real-time agents; misspelled sosa:simpleResult.
Observations and results subclassed per quantity (TemperatureObservation, TemperatureResult); qudt:QuantityValue and geo:Geometry declared subclasses of sosa:Result; stored in Neo4j.
A Part-Observation-Property design pattern; farm operations with input and output products via ssn:hasInput/ssn:hasOutput.
Observations kept as rows of a time-series database with sosa:madeBySensor, quantity, unit, value and timestamp columns, federated with Brick/BOT graphs.

Sensors and algorithms point to OBOE characteristics (orka:observesCharacteristic) rather than sosa:observes; a SWRL rule makes the hosting robot the feature of interest of proprioceptor observations.
ssn:System given an ethics mode (:hasEthicMode) and privacy attributes from ColPri; SEAS connections between systems.
Aggregators typed dashb:AggregatedObservableProperty; units and data types on a separate metric node; sensor annotations on a Web Thing gateway drive dashboards.
Metadata nodes attached to observations (mmo:hasMetadata, mmo:Frequency); a SWRL rule infers ssn:isProxyFor from a stimulus; SOSA terms written in the ssn namespace.
Measurement and Instrument subclass sosa:Observation and sosa:Sensor; diagnoses as prov:Activity over measurements; designed for relational databases.
Reuses a non-existent sosa:ObservationValue; actuations are HTTP requests with OWL-S preconditions and effects for AI planning.
dcat:Dataset declared a subclass of sosa:Result to point to files and external databases (dcat:DataService) from observations.
Signals (time series kept outside the graph) are attached to hosted devices by properties such as ev:ActivePower and queried with a SPARQL extension instead of observations.
IRIs built from relational primary keys of the WoSIS database; SPARQL queries over SOSA graphs used to generate a SensorThings API.
Actuator modules linked to agricultural properties by ssn:forProperty; observations named by kind (NDVIObservation) as individuals.
Signal classes carry OWL restrictions on their sensor and unit; sensors and actuators are classes linked by sosa:isObservedBy/isActedBy restrictions.
Shortcut roles (speed, pos, acceleration) defined by role chains hosts • madeObservation • hasResult from a platform to measured values.
Mapping of the FIESTA-IoT ontology (old SSN) to OMA NGSI context entities.
Quality-of-context indicators (precision, freshness) attached to observation results.
Provenance (prov:wasGeneratedBy) held at the observation-collection level; flow paths between subsystems by downstreamOf.
The measurement capability of the sensor is linked to the feature of interest of the observation.
Measurements hang off asset states (AssetState → Measurement) with an uncertainty value; measurement IRIs embed probe and timestamp.

SensorThings API entities mapped to SOSA with OWL functional and inverse-functional constraints to detect inconsistencies; result and unit arrays of MultiDatastreams lose their pairing when flattened.
ssn:observedProperty given on raster scientific field layers (ex:BaseLayer with rows, cols, WKT bbox) rather than on observations.
Alignment only: weather station deployment details aligned with ssn:Deployment, co-iot entities with ssn:Platform; m3-lite quantity kinds reused.
Time granularity terms invented in the ssn namespace (ssn:Day, ssn:Hour).
Security metadata (access control, authentication provider) attached to IoT-Stream streams generated by SOSA sensors.
A processing step loosely linked to sosa:Observation and sosa:Sample, Procedure being judged broader.
Ground motion represented as sampled time steps with a quantity kind and a direction (NS, EW, V).
Observable properties modelled as a DUL:Role that an object property plays given the sensing capabilities, not as an intrinsic quality.
SOSA classes referenced from OpenAPI schemas by an x-refersTo annotation (a smart door as sosa:Actuator).
Planning agents aligned with sosa:Platform, with location and time on agent states.
A hosts property relates a welding machine to the part it welds; whether it is sosa:hosts is not shown.
The work's ContextAttribute class is declared equivalent to sosa:Observation.
System capabilities (operating power range, response time, measurement range) describe the sensors.
A human observer (foaf:Person) is the sosa:Sensor; the procedure forest_mensuration is a sosa:Procedure. Experimental plots are seen as sosa:Sample.
Multimedia results (sosa:Result subclass) decomposed into temporal and spatial segments carrying MPEG-7-style descriptors, aligned with the Media Resource ontology.
Observation classes per property kind, restricted with owl:allValuesFrom on sosa:observedProperty; static property values attached directly to the property (osph:hasPropertySimpleValue).

Observation types are subclasses of sosa:Observation with OWL restrictions on result, observed property and usedProcedure; laboratory procedures are both sosa:Procedure and skos:Concept; alignments with ISO 19156.
An animal (southern elephant seal) is the sosa:Platform; location is itself observed, with a WKT geometry as the result.

Static design properties carry value and unit directly (brick:value, brick:hasUnit) instead of observations; sensors point to external time series by ID (Brick ref:hasTimeseriesID). SHACL shapes validate sosa:Actuator descriptions.

Each VSS signal becomes a property class with matching sensor/actuator classes; vehicle branches are features of interest. Contextual driving facts (traffic flow, visibility) are modelled as observations.
Proposes to treat sosa:Observation, sosa:Actuation and sosa:Sampling as subclasses of dcat:Dataset to attach DUV user feedback for a GEO label.
Uses the 2009 SSN (observationResultTime, SensorOutput) with DUL; property values are also stored on entity properties (hasValue) with the observation time.
Observations carry a trust score (ts) and a description target; JSON-LD messages per spatial entity.
Micro-controllers are subclasses of ssn:System implementing sosa:Procedures (algorithms); WoT TD aligned with td:Thing subclass of ssn:System and td:InteractionPattern subclass of sosa:Procedure.
Observations are also typed void:Dataset; collections are aggregated recursively along spatial, temporal and property dimensions.
ssn:observes links a service or its telemetry to a seas:Process rather than a sensor to a property.
Rules over observations infer domain facts (an area with high CO becomes :OffLimitArea); SHACL schemas over SOSA triple patterns.

SSN/SOSA classes re-classified under BFO/CCO (sosa:FeatureOfInterest under an information content entity, ObservableProperty under bfo:quality); sensor kinds defined as subclasses (temperature sensor, pressure sensor).

Uses non-existent SOSA terms (sosa:madeObservation, sosa:hasObservableProperty, sosa:isObservedBy) and ssn:Device as a subclass of ssn:System; a controller regulates observable properties (priv:controls).
Automatic ontology alignment maps aras:Sensor to sosa:Sensor.
One observation node per sensor acts as a template (no result value, no time) holding the real-time data key and topic; time series stay outside the graph.
Data-quality tags attached to observations (hasObservationTag) and a CorrectedValue subclass of ssn:ObservationValue linked by hasCorrectedValue; SWRL rules classify suspect data.
An extra PO2:hasObjectOfInterest names the object observed within the feature; sensors and actuators may be human agents (a tasting panel).

Dataset-level metadata model: dcat:Dataset linked to sosa:ObservationCollection, with FeatureTheme and PropertyTheme SKOS concepts as thematic abstractions beside FeatureOfInterest and ObservableProperty.
The result of a web service call (a Yelp search) is wrapped as a sosa observation blank node by a JavaScript accessor.
Reuses sosa:madeObservation and sosa:observes in a manufacturing ontology; machines 'host' tools in the prose.
Observation classes defined in DL (HighTrafficObservation, ∃observedProperty.CongestionLevel) and inferred by cascading stream reasoning.
Invents ssn:-prefixed data properties for weather variables (ssn:Temperature, ssn:WindSpeed, ssn:relativehumidity) and object properties (ssn:area).
Design choices from an alignment exercise: ssn:Property used in place of sosa:ObservableProperty, sosa:isHostedBy linking a sensor to the room it is installed in.

Alternative observation designs: mssn:AltObservationDesign subclass of ssn:Observation, with refined altFeatureOfInterest, altObservedProperty and altObservedBy to flag multiple mappings of one dataset.
Observation subclasses defined by OWL class expressions (NursePresentObservation, SoundAboveThresholdFault) so that reasoning classifies observations into faults and nurse calls.
SHACL SPARQL rules built from automatic alignments rewrite oneM2M and OCF data into SOSA observations.
Sensor-centred triples (sensor hasUnit, hasQuantityKind, hasResult) in the work's MIoT-Ont namespace, without observation individuals.
Rules as SPARQL CONSTRUCT stored in RDF (SPIN-like rso:) classify observations (health:Healthy); misspelled ssn:observerBy.
SOSA terms re-declared as a PROV extension (prov-sw:) so that observations are prov:Activity associated with the sensor and generating the result.
SWRL rules over observation results flag abnormal vital signs; a vital sign is linked to its observations by an own VitalSignhasObservation property.
sosa:hasSimpleResult used with a structured QUDT node instead of a literal.
Attributes of geographic entities in a narrative map are modelled as observations grouped per entity in a collection whose feature is the map content item.
The ontology evolves from the sensor data stream, under a consistency model for updates and new concepts.
Calibration models (OM plus Content MathML) attached to sensors through a new calibratedSensor class; measures with metrological uncertainty.
RDF-star annotates a sensor's hasSimpleResult statement with a certainty value (ex:probability), aggregated by weighted average.
sosa:resultTime drives window membership of LDP stream containers.
Observations are evidence (EvidenceObservation) clustered into maintained hazard events; one feature of interest per incoming bundle.
A whole observing campaign (EHT VLBI) is one sosa:Observation linked to an observatory and to observational data.
GEO label facets are computed from SOSA/SSN graphs, e.g. user feedback attached to a sosa:Observation with duv:hasUserFeedback.
Observations are indexed into a time-series store by declared predicate patterns (value, time, sensor, reading type).
Sensor kinds of the pilot (fibre-optic, acceleration) defined as subclasses of sosa:Sensor.
Discusses aligning SAREF with SOSA, e.g. saref:BuildingSpace as a subclass of sosa:Platform.
An own property (p:sourceStation) links an observation to the weather station it comes from instead of madeBySensor.
Satellite subsystems are subclasses of sosa:Platform, generated automatically from channel lists.
Feature-of-interest subclasses are used to derive a category tree of marketplace offerings.
An own ca:MeasurementCode (e.g. ca:TMAX-d combining quantity, aggregation and sampling interval) plays the role of sosa:ObservableProperty, without using SOSA.
Laptop hardware components (temperature, pressure, humidity sensors) reuse sosa:Sensor subclasses in a digital product passport ontology.
A capability ontology (C4I) is aligned with SSN through a separate bridging module (C4I2SSN).
